html:
The Church of Saint Simeon Stylites is a huge ruined church in the hills west of Aleppo, built around 475 to 491 around the pillar on which the hermit Simeon had lived for decades.

Simeon, a monk, climbed a pillar near the village in about 423 to escape the crowds, and stayed on top until his death in 459, praying and preaching. Pilgrims came from across the Roman world, and other "pillar saints" copied him. After his death a cross-shaped church of four basilicas was built around the pillar, one of the largest churches of its age.

It stands among the Dead Cities, hundreds of abandoned stone villages of late Roman Syria, a World Heritage Site since 2011. The church was damaged in the Syrian civil war. See also Christianity.
sum: The Church of Saint Simeon Stylites is a huge ruined church in the hills west of Aleppo, built around 475 to 491 around the pillar on which the hermit Simeon had lived for decades.
